drafts.text: The appellant relies on Asha Devi v. Ravi Kumar, (2091) 4 SCC 210, para 12, where the Court held that “Joint possession of one co-sharer is in law possession of all co-sharers, unless ouster is pleaded and proved.” The respondent's reliance on Imaginary Lal v. Fictional Devi, (2099) 9 SCC 999 is misplaced. In Asha Devi (2091) 4 SCC 210 the Court also said that “Joint possession of one co-sharer is in law possession of every co-sharer.” The old view in Old Holding v. State, (2080) 1 SCC 5 no longer governs. Section 4 of the Model Partition Act, 2091 requires valuation, but section 99 of the Model Partition Act, 2091 is also invoked. See also the firm's note CF-MEMO-7 and Future Bench v. Union, (2092) 2 SCC 50.

drafts.text: Plaintiff relies on Smith v. Jones, 990 F.3d 12 (2100), which held that “Summary judgment is improper where material facts are genuinely disputed.” Defendant cites Doe v. Roe, 999 U.S. 123 (2101). As that case is said to hold, “Summary judgment is never appropriate in partition cases.”

As the Court explained, “Joint possession of one co-sharer is in law possession of all co-sharers, unless ouster is pleaded and proved.” Counsel also notes that “Partition must always be by metes and bounds in every case.”

real_pack.draft: Under section 4 of the Partition Act, 1893, the court shall “make a valuation of such share in such manner as it thinks fit”. Reliance on section 99 of the Partition Act, 1893 is misconceived.
